A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same FedCBDR research. Their text, equations, tables, figures, appendices, and checklists are readable and support comparison, including matching material moved between the appendix and main text.

before.justification: v2 reports original classification experiments on CIFAR10, CIFAR100, and TinyImageNet, including baseline comparisons, ablations, sensitivity analyses, and case studies.

after.justification: v4 retains these original experiments and adds scalability results and computation and communication measurements in Appendix A.1.7.

M1.justification: The GDR sampling procedure, TTS loss, training stages, Equations 1–9, and Algorithm 1 are unchanged. Moving the pseudocode into the main text and evaluating additional client configurations do not establish a method revision.

E1.justification: All three datasets and classification tasks are retained. Appendix A.1.7 adds a CIFAR10/CIFAR100 scenario described as asynchronous participation with a 0.2 client sampling rate, extending coverage beyond the earlier full-participation evaluations.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged in every matched experiment. The new scalability comparison reuses FedLwF, LANDER, and Re-Fed; it introduces no new comparison method. FedAvg is mentioned as an overhead reference without a corresponding reported comparator row.

E3.justification: The new scalability evaluation specifies five tasks, 0.2 client sampling, and additional replay budgets. Table 10 reports 50-client results, although the prose mentions 50/100 clients and gives CIFAR10 replay budgets inconsistent with the table labels. Existing experimental settings are retained.

E4.justification: Appendix A.1.7 adds scalability and computation/communication analyses. Figure 4 revises the existing temperature and weight sensitivity evidence, and Figure 6 replaces two airplane attention maps. The component ablations and other existing supplementary analyses remain unchanged.

E5.justification: Both versions retain three-seed means and standard deviations for the main comparisons and seed 2023 for the ten-client tables. The new tables introduce no additional run-count disclosure, uncertainty estimation, or significance testing; Figure 4 retains boxplot reporting.

E6.justification: Figure 4 replaces all four sensitivity distributions, shifting displayed accuracies from approximately 43–51% to 54–65% despite retaining the CIFAR100 experimental caption. Figure 6 changes two attention maps while retaining their displayed logits. Tables 10–11 add scalability and resource-cost results. All retained table values match, so these changes do not establish improved performance in the original benchmark comparisons.

T1.justification: Appendix A.1.7 adds asymptotic cost statements: O(n_k d^2) for client-side ISVD and O(N d^2) for server-side SVD, with N equal to the total pseudo-feature count. No derivation or proof accompanies them; the existing mathematical formulation is unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same GDR/TTS contributions, class-balancing and privacy claims, and headline 2%–15% accuracy improvement over six methods. The additional experiments do not redefine these core claims.

C2.justification: v4 removes the explicit conclusion that sampling under globally imbalanced distributions remains an open problem, replacing it with a general reference to more complex scenarios. Appendix A.1.7 also adds the interpretation that SVD and leverage-score overhead is relatively small.

D1.justification: Table 11 newly documents samples per client, feature dimensions, ISVD and feature-extraction timings, and upload/download volumes. The added scalability section supplies participation and replay settings, albeit inconsistently. Existing optimizer, hardware, and supplementary-code disclosures are unchanged.

R1.justification: v4 adds 19 references covering broader FL applications, lifelong person re-identification, and future extension topics, and removes the 2022 Practical lossless federated singular vector decomposition citation. These changes broaden citations without substantially rewriting the central positioning against replay and distillation methods.

P1.justification: Limited edits add an FL-application sentence, an affiliation, acknowledgments, and the new appendix subsection. Algorithm and dataset material move into the main text, with corresponding appendix restructuring. Most existing explanatory prose remains unchanged.

P2.justification: Tables 10–11 are added, while Algorithm 1 and the dataset-statistics table move from the appendix into the main text. Figure 4 is redrawn with different vertical scales, and two Figure 6 heatmaps are replaced. The remaining displays largely retain their design.

improvement.justification: The added participation/scalability tests and resource accounting provide useful practical evidence. However, Figure 4 replaces results under an unchanged caption, Table 10 conflicts with the stated replay budgets, and Table 11 reports a 1.2952-second total against listed components of 0.00452 and 1.0250 seconds. The PDFs do not resolve these discrepancies or explain the figure replacements, preventing a reliable judgment of net quality improvement.
